output_text: description: Definitive guidelines for building secure, performant, maintainable apps on Cloudflare’s developer platform. Emphasize tiny bundles, edge-first design, robust security. Prefer Workers & Pages for all new applications. Use official `wrangler` CLI for scaffolding/deploy; ✅ GOOD: Always start with `wrangler generate`. `npx wrangler generate my-worker --type=module --ts` ; `npx create-cloudflare@latest my-fullstack-app --framework next`. Monorepos: For multiple Workers/Pages apps use `pnpm` or `yarn workspaces`. ✅ GOOD: Centralize dependencies/build scripts. `"workspaces": ["apps/*", "packages/*"]`. Environment Variables: Manage secrets via `wrangler.toml` or Cloudflare dashboard; use `.dev.vars` for local dev. ❌ BAD: Storing sensitive data directly in code or `.env` files that aren't `.dev.vars`. ✅ GOOD: Define in `wrangler.toml` and reference in Worker. `name = "my-worker"` `main = "src/index.ts"` `MY_API_KEY = "your-api-key-value" # For non-sensitive defaults or local testing` `[secrets]` ✅ GOOD: Use `.dev.vars` for local secrets and CLI integration. `DATABASE_URL="postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/mydb"` `dotenv -e .dev.vars -- npx prisma migrate dev`. Edge-first: Workers stateless; avoid in-memory state needing persistence. ❌ BAD: Relying on global variables for user sessions/shared data. `let requestCount = 0; // This will reset or be inconsistent` `async fetch(request, env, ctx) { return new Response(\`Requests: ${requestCount}\`); }` ✅ GOOD: Use KV/D1/Durable Objects. KV example uses `env.REQUEST_COUNTER.get/put`. Serverless SQL: Use D1 for new relational DBs; existing regional DBs use Hyperdrive. ✅ GOOD: D1. Example: `import { DrizzleD1Database, drizzle } from 'drizzle-orm/d1';` `interface
